review_notes:
I reviewed the whole of Mathlib/Order/Sublocale.lean against the repeated-proof-machinery rubric. I did not open any other files, and I did not run Lean.

The closest match is the range characterisation of `Sublocale.toNucleus`. It appears twice:
- `range_toNucleus` proves `ext x; constructor; · simp +contextual [eq_comm]; · intro hx; exact ⟨x, by simp_all⟩`.
- `nucleusIsoSublocale.right_inv` proves `ext x; simpa using ⟨by simp +contextual [eq_comm], fun hx ↦ ⟨x, by simp [hx]⟩⟩`.

Both are the same two-direction argument. A point of the range is a fixed point of the restriction map, and a member `x` of `S` is its own image. Each version is only a one-line simp call per direction. A shared lemma would save almost nothing, and I did not verify that `right_inv` could simply reuse `range_toNucleus`. I judged this to be short routine simp reasoning, which the rubric excludes, so I do not report it.

I also looked at the following and found them either not repeated or too thin to count:
- the `restrictAux` and `giAux` unfoldings;
- `map_sSup'` and `map_top'` in `restrict`;
- `iInf_mem`, `infClosed` and `top_mem`;
- the instance definitions.

The `sInf_mem` / `himp_mem` closure arguments appear once each, in `Nucleus.toSublocale`.
